scope: Proposition 6.1 (Contact-value descent on the square) of the manuscript “Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture” (preprints/Contact-Fano-manifolds-and-the-LeBrun-Salamon-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 062 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c7ef1ec44ffd8d7a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X be a smooth simply connected complex projective contact Fano manifold with Pic(X) = Z[L]. Assume that a family of free contact lines covers a dense open subset of X. Let p : Y → Z be dominant, where Y is a proper integral algebraic space over C. Suppose that there are regular sections W12 ∈ H0(︁ Y, p∗ (TX ⊠ L) )︁ , W21 ∈ H0(︁ Y, p∗ (L ⊠ TX) )︁ with the same contact value ξ = (θ ⊠ 1)(W12) = (1 ⊠ θ)(W21) ∈ H0 (Y, p∗ M). (6.1) Then there is a unique section B ∈ H0(Z, M) such that p∗B = ξ.
